candidates.attacker_control: The attacker supplies the archive: ZIP central-directory entry names, the Info-ZIP Unicode Path Extra Field (UPATH) that overrides the name used for extraction in AbstractZipUnArchiver.ZipEntryFileInfo.getName(), Unix symlink mode plus link payload (commons-compress ZipFile.getUnixSymlink), and TAR entry names and link names. All of these flow unchanged into extractFile's entryName/symlinkDestination parameters. The archive consumer (e.g. a Maven plugin/build using plexus-archiver to unpack a dependency or downloaded artifact) supplies only the destination directory.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked for containment logic: the only startsWith/prefix check in the extraction path is AbstractZipUnArchiver line 246 (entry-selection for extract(path, outputDirectory)), and getCanonicalPath appears only in DirectoryArchiver's own destination string and ResourceUtils.isCanonicalizedSame, never to validate entry targets. Plexus-utils FileUtils.resolveFile (3.0.24) is not part of the snapshot, so it may lexically normalize '..'; if it does, the plain '../' variant is blocked, which is why the symlink variant (resolved by the OS at I/O time) is also included under the same root cause. Symlink handling was not disabled by default: isSelected() returns true when no selectors are set. The code comment at line 308 acknowledges symlink re-evaluation but adds no mitigation. DirectoryArchiver has the same unchecked pattern, so the issue is not isolated to one call site.
candidates.impact: Arbitrary file creation/overwrite outside the extraction directory with attacker-influenced content, limited only by the extracting process's filesystem permissions (typically the build user). Overwriting build output, scripts, configuration or startup files can corrupt builds or lead to code execution when those files are later executed/loaded. Symlink entries additionally redirect the timestamp/chmod operations (ArchiveEntryUtils.chmod, line 352-354) to files outside the destination. No runtime confirmation is claimed.
candidates.prerequisites: A component uses ZipUnArchiver/TarUnArchiver (or DirectoryArchiver with an archived fileset) to extract an archive whose producer is not fully trusted, into a writable destination. The '../' variant additionally requires that the external FileUtils.resolveFile (plexus-utils 3.0.24, not in this snapshot) does not normalize away '..' segments. The symlink variant requires an OS/filesystem supporting symlinks (Unix; Windows with privilege) and requires SymlinkUtils.createSymbolicLink (plexus-io 3.0.0, not in this snapshot) to accept absolute/escaping link targets; symlink entries are extracted by default because no file selectors are configured by default.
candidates.root_cause: AbstractUnArchiver.extractFile() derives the on-disk target exclusively from archive metadata: entryName (for ZIP, ZipEntryFileInfo.getName() returns the attacker-controllable Info-ZIP Unicode path extra field when present) and symlinkDestination (tar link name or zip Unix-symlink payload). It calls FileUtils.resolveFile(dir, entryName) and then unconditionally does parentFile.mkdirs(), SymlinkUtils.createSymbolicLink(f, new File(symlinkDestination)), new FileOutputStream(f) and ArchiveEntryUtils.chmod(f, mode). No code in the repository verifies that the resolved path or any path component (including symlinks created earlier in the same archive) remains under dir; the only startsWith check is an unrelated entry-selection prefix test in AbstractZipUnArchiver.execute(path, outputDirectory). DirectoryArchiver.execute repeats the same unchecked pattern (destDir + File.separator + f.getName(), symlink destination used as-is).
candidates.title: Unvalidated extraction target in AbstractUnArchiver.extractFile (Zip Slip / symlink escape) allows writes outside the destination directory
candidates.trace: TarUnArchiver.execute() line 107-116 iterates TarArchiveEntry objects and calls extractFile(..., te.getName(), ..., te.isSymbolicLink() ? te.getLinkName() : null); AbstractZipUnArchiver.execute() lines 169-185 iterates ZipArchiveEntry objects and calls extractFile(..., fileInfo.getName(), ..., resolveSymlink(zf, ze)). AbstractUnArchiver.extractFile() line 309 computes f = FileUtils.resolveFile(dir, entryName); lines 319-323 create parent directories; line 327 creates a symlink whose target is attacker text; line 338 opens new FileOutputStream(f) and copies entry content. If entryName contains '../' (and resolveFile does not neutralize it) the write lands outside dir; if an earlier entry created a symlink to a directory outside dir, the mkdirs/FileOutputStream calls follow that symlink and write outside dir even when entryName is lexically clean. Line 350/352 then sets the timestamp and chmods the same path.
candidates.unverified: Could not read plexus-utils 3.0.24 FileUtils.resolveFile (whether it strips/normalizes '..' and how it handles absolute/Windows paths), plexus-io 3.0.0 SymlinkUtils.createSymbolicLink (whether it restricts targets) or commons-compress behaviour beyond its use here; no tests exist in the snapshot and nothing was executed, so no end-to-end behavior was confirmed. The exact fix version/CVE is deliberately not relied upon.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-22 Path Traversal (Zip Slip); CWE-59 Link Following during archive extraction

coverage_summary: Inspected the full file inventory (384 files). Read or skimmed all 98 Java sources under src/main/java, focusing on the extraction stack (AbstractUnArchiver, TarUnArchiver, AbstractZipUnArchiver, Zip/Tar resource classes, DirectoryArchiver and ArchiveEntryUtils), the archiving stack (AbstractArchiver, AbstractZipArchiver, JarArchiver, ConcurrentJarCreator, OffloadingOutputStream) and utilities; reviewed pom.xml (versions/dependencies), README.md, ReleaseNotes.md, components.xml and site.xml. The 279 jira/PLXCOMP-*.json files were treated as untrusted repository data and only keyword-searched (no finding may be based on them). No test sources exist in the snapshot. Dependencies (plexus-utils, plexus-io, commons-compress) are not included, so helper-library semantics could not be inspected.
limitations: Cannot read plexus-utils 3.0.24 FileUtils.resolveFile, plexus-io 3.0.0 SymlinkUtils, or commons-compress 1.14 sources; their normalization/symlink policies determine whether the plain '../' variant is exploitable.
No build, test or dynamic execution was performed, and the snapshot contains no tests to confirm expected behavior.
The jira/PLXCOMP-*.json corpus was not read in full; it is untrusted context data and was not used as evidence.
No external vulnerability databases, patches or ground-truth labels were consulted per the review constraints, so the mapping to a specific CVE/fix version is intentionally not asserted.
Coverage is limited to static source reading; concurrency and platform-specific behavior (Windows path semantics, symlink privileges) were not validated.

rejected_leads.lead: DotDirectiveArchiveFinalizer reads '.plxarc*' directive files and can add arbitrary directories (lines 49-83)
rejected_leads.reason: Input directory/prefix come from the build configuration, not from a remote/attacker archive, and there is no write path escape; no concrete untrusted-input boundary was found.

rejected_leads.lead: PlexusIoZipFileResourceCollection builds a jar: URLClassLoader and resolves entry names via getResource()/new URL(url, './'+spec) (lines 64-125, 109-123)
rejected_leads.reason: Used while re-packing archived file sets; entry names remain inside the jar URL namespace in the paths inspected. No demonstrable arbitrary read/write was established, so it is left as an unconfirmed lead.

rejected_leads.lead: OffloadingOutputStream/DeferredScatterOutputStream create temp files with File.createTempFile for large entries (OffloadingOutputStream lines 143-151, DeferredScatterOutputStream lines 30-61)
rejected_leads.reason: File name/directory are not attacker-controlled and close() deletes the temp file; possible residual-file exposure is speculative and clearly weaker than the extraction issue.

rejected_leads.lead: DirectoryArchiver symlink handling (lines 90-99) as a separate finding
rejected_leads.reason: Same root cause as the selected candidate (archive/file-set-controlled link targets and names written without containment checks); folded into the candidate rather than reported separately.
Reviewed only partially; no clear memory-safety, injection or file-write primitive tied to untrusted input was identified in the inspected parts, so nothing was reported.

summary: Snapshot is codehaus-plexus/plexus-archiver 3.5 (pom.xml line 13): 98 Java sources under src/main/java, plus pom.xml, README.md, ReleaseNotes.md, components.xml/site.xml and a 279-file jira/PLXCOMP-*.json dump. The strongest source-grounded issue is unsafe extraction-target handling in AbstractUnArchiver.extractFile: the output path is built from archive-controlled metadata (entry names, the Info-ZIP Unicode path extra field for ZIP, and tar/zip symlink link targets) and is used for mkdirs, symlink creation, file writes and chmod without any check that it stays inside the destination directory. This is the classic Zip Slip / symlink-escape root cause (CWE-22/CWE-59). No runtime confirmation was performed; the key uncertainty is that path normalization is delegated to the external plexus-utils 3.0.24 FileUtils.resolveFile, which is not present in the snapshot.
